 Part 4 Nutrition Therapy
Introduction:
78-year-old Caucasian female diagnosed with Parkinson’s
disease ten years ago—currently treated with Sinemet.
She recently moved from her assisted living apartment to 
a skilled care facility. She states: “Every time I eat, it feels 
like it gets stuck in my throat. I am scared that I will choke.” 
Patient was determined to have dysphagia secondary to her
Parkinson’s disease.
Rx: Sinemet: carbidopa/levodopa, 50/200 mg controlled
release tablet BID
1. How is the pathophysiology of Parkinson’s related to her
development of dysphagia?
2. How does her medication, Sinemet, assist with control
of her disease?
